topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture series and sets out what students should learn from this lecture.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This material establishes cancer development as a stepwise accumulation of cellular changes and identifies the questions that this model raises.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue organisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why understanding cancer requires studying cells within the organised tissue context that isolated cell cultures cannot fully reproduce.

topics.label: Invasion and metastasis as features of malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how malignant tumours differ from benign tumours through invasion of surrounding tissue and the capacity to spread to distant sites.

topics.label: Tumour progression and the clinical significance of benign tumours
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the transition from benign to malignant growth while explaining why benign status guarantees neither progression nor harmlessness.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how tumour names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming rules.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how tumour growth disrupts normal bodily function and how widespread metastases can produce fatal organ failure.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency and distribution of tumour types across populations and species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the rationale for detecting cancer early and assess how effectively screening can achieve this in different tumour types.

topics.label: Lecture close and upcoming practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns students to the learning outcomes and directs them towards revision and forthcoming teaching.
